analysis.title: Our Thoughts on the NVDA CEO Situation
key_insights: Wolfe had stayed silent on the NVDA CEO situation due to the nature of the press coverage. A NY Times report on the evening of 11/11 that the CEO also had an affair with a subordinate executive at NVDA changes that.

Wolfe still thinks the board will make its best efforts to keep the CEO, but the new allegations make that more challenging. Media reported the board was meeting on 11/11, and Wolfe thinks an announcement is possible as early as 11/12.

If the CEO is asked to step down, Wolfe sees zero impact on fundamentals or earnings through at least CY28, because NVDA is mainly sold out through that period. A CEO transition would have no impact on orders or the roadmap, which runs well through CY28.

Wolfe calls export control worries in media reports misplaced. NVDA's AI shipments to China are now de minimis. NVDA has US government permission to ship the H200 into China, but the Chinese government has restricted use by Chinese companies, so further export controls would have no effect.

Wolfe says the CEO represents key person risk because Huang identified where AI was going and let NVDA get there first. Wolfe cannot easily identify anyone currently at NVDA who could step into the role. News reports suggest the board is already working with an outside firm to identify replacement candidates.
NVDA's IP library, software advantage and engineering talent would not leave with the CEO. Wolfe thinks Huang's legacy would drive a lingering competitive advantage even without his leadership.

Wolfe says a CEO departure would show up in NVDA's multiple. The size of the discount is very difficult to gauge, but the stock is under 8x Wolfe's FY29 earnings power, so much of the impact may already be priced in.

market_movers.rationale: Outperform and $275 target against a $173.73 price on 11/11/26 (58.3% upside). Wolfe sees no fundamental impact from a CEO change through CY28, and the stock is under 8x FY29 earnings power.
